- **Economy:** Not confirmed by this survey.
- **Ethnic composition:** Not confirmed by this survey.
- **Religious denominations:** Calvary Cemetery (Marshall) church records and a St. Paul's Icelandic Lutheran Church series (Minneota) appear in the catalog; the Marshall congregations are not otherwise confirmed.
- **Key historical events:** Not confirmed by this survey.
- **Coverage of this survey:** Marshall has 6 digitized volumes, all listed (total 6, complete); Lyon County as a whole has 82 volumes, of which the survey listed the first page only.

args.guideSection:
## Research tips
- **Search order:** Start with the Lyon County Clerk of District Court, which holds birth and death records from 1874 (per [Lyon County, Minnesota Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lyon_County,_Minnesota_Genealogy)), then the statewide FamilySearch indexes: Minnesota Death Index 1908-2002 (collection 1937234), Minnesota Deaths 1887-2001 (3398461), and Minnesota Death Records and Certificates 1900-1955 (2477957). Then check the Marshall obituaries: the 1985 volumes and obituary indexes 1873-1953 on FamilySearch, which are name-indexed but not full-text searchable. Browse-only or offline sources come last.
- Minnesota's statewide death indexes are free to search on FamilySearch, but index entries do not themselves establish a place of death; confirm the death place from the certificate or an obituary.
- **Obituaries:** The Minnesota Obituaries 1865-2006 collection (2469546) is on FamilySearch; the Southwest Minnesota Historical Center obituary file index (catalog 408979), Southwest State University obituary files (409008), and Prairieland Genealogical Society obituary files (1197876) and index cards (1197864) are offline, catalogued for Marshall, Minnesota ([Marshall County, Minnesota Genealogy, Obituaries](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Marshall_County,_Minnesota_Genealogy#Obituaries)). Note this wiki page is for Marshall County; the catalog entries name Marshall, Minnesota in Lyon County.
- **Cemetery:** The Marshall Cemetery alphabetized index (catalog koha:525977, FamilySearch Library) is a typescript, about 1992; its three numeric columns are unexplained. The Calvary Cemetery records microfilm (catalog koha:390369) includes death entries 1898-1925 and cemetery records ca. 1900-1990; it is at the FamilySearch Library, Granite Mountain Record Vault (storage), and online at FamilySearch Centers and affiliate libraries.
- **Church records:** Minnesota church records are incomplete online ([Minnesota Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Minnesota_Church_Records)); the parish or denomination for Calvary is unconfirmed.
- **Alternative sources:** Veterans Grave Registration Reports 1930-1975 (4489446) apply only if the decedent was a veteran. Minnesota Will Records 1849-1985 (1607922) may hold a probate file.
- **Finding aids:** Lyon County Courthouse, 607 W Main St, Marshall MN 56258, phone 507-537-6734, with the county website at http://www.lyonco.org/. A negative online result is not absence: the record may be undigitized, unindexed, or held only at the courthouse.

Statewide registration start date conflicts within the Wiki: the Texas Vital Records page states statewide registration of births and deaths began in 1903 with the formation of the Texas Department of Public Health (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Texas_Vital_Records); the Texas Research Tips page states statewide registration began in 1908 and was generally complied with by the 1930s (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Texas_Research_Tips_and_Strategies). Both are reported; the 1903 date is the one on the vital-records page.

Local registration: the Texas Research Tips page states that as early as 1873 some cities and towns authorized registration of births and deaths; it does not name the towns, so a city or county death record for 1962-2024 must be checked against the city or county of death.

Period gap: the Texas Death Index 1964-1998 collection begins in 1964, so deaths in 1962-1963 are not covered by the name index in this survey; the Texas Deaths 1977-1986 and 1890-1977 image collections were the only listed death image sets overlapping the period, and no death collection listed here covers 1999-2024.

The Texas Deaths 1890-1977 collection is titled by its catalog range; the Texas Vital Records page gives the FamilySearch death image collection as 1890-1976. Use the collection's own title and years when citing it.

Death-certificate images for 1903-1982 are offered by Ancestry on a subscription basis (Texas Online Genealogy Records page, https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Texas_Online_Genealogy_Records); the FamilySearch death collections above are index-and-image or index-only as their rows state.

Cross-border: the survey returned no neighboring-county list for Texas; search adjoining states only where the death place is near a border, and do not assume a Texas death record is held in another state's series.
Death records do not show the same county or city everywhere; a Texas death certificate's place must be checked as the place of death, which this survey cannot confirm for the capture's county.

args.guideSection:
## Research tips
- **Search order:** Start with FamilySearch's Texas Death Index, 1964-1998 (collection 1375599; index only, free), since it is the only listed index that covers the period from 1964. Then search Texas Deaths, 1977-1986 (collection 1930157; index and images, free), and Texas Death Index, 1903-2000 (collection 1949337; index only, free) to cover the whole period. Texas Deaths, 1890-1977 (collection 1983324) and Texas Deaths and Burials, 1903-1973 (collection 1681049) overlap the early years of the period and are free on FamilySearch.
- **Gap at the start of the period:** the name indexes begin in 1964 and the image collections end in 1977 or 1986. Deaths in 1962-1963 are not covered by the listed index; check the image collection 1983324 and then the Bureau of Vital Statistics.
- **Gap after 1986 for images:** the survey listed no FamilySearch death image collection covering 1987-2024. For deaths after 1998 the survey returned only the 1903-2000 index and Ancestry's subscription collections; for an image, order the certificate from the state (http://www.dshs.state.tx.us/vs/default.shtm), which the Texas Vital Records page directs requesters to (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Texas_Vital_Records).
- **Jurisdiction-specific advice:** The Texas Research Tips page notes that death records from 1903 onward asked for the deceased's birth and parent information, though accuracy depended on relatives' memory (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Texas_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- **Naming conventions:** The United States Naming Customs page returned only links to abbreviation and name-variation guides, so no Texas-specific naming practice was confirmed (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/United_States_Naming_Customs).
- **Alternative sources when primary records are missing:** obituaries, church records (incomplete; Texas, Church Records, 1852-1994, collection 2790180), cemetery interment cards for Dallas County (collection 3656813) and Harris County Hollywood Cemetery records (collection 2040173). Cite the county-level cemetery sets only for their named counties.
- **Finding aids:** the Texas Record Finder and the Guided Research page for Texas births, marriages and deaths are named on the Texas Research Tips page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Texas_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- **Place-of-death check:** The survey cannot confirm the county or city of death for the uploaded Texas death certificate capture. Its place must be read from the capture itself before any county series is searched.

- The original County of Los Angeles covered parts of what are now Kern, San Bernardino, Riverside and Orange counties. San Bernardino County split off in 1853, Kern in 1866, and Orange in 1889; in 1893 part of San Bernardino County that had been Los Angeles territory became part of Riverside County (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Los_Angeles_County,_California_Genealogy).
- Before the county existed, the records were at city or Franciscan mission places (same page, Boundary Changes).
- For a 1962-2024 death in Los Angeles County, the county boundary itself is stable in the sources read; the 1850s-1890s changes do not bear on this period.

entry.rationale: Statewide Texas death index (Texas, Death Index, 1964-1998, collection 1375599) is name-searchable and is the state index to read first for deaths after 1964 (loc_002). It gives a death year and county to test against the Texas capture and the 1962 move to Los Angeles. An index entry does not by itself establish the place of death; confirm from a certificate or other record.

entry.repository: other: local upload of Texas death certificate capture (uploads/ancestry-texas-death-cert-quass.pdf)
entry.rationale: Read the place of death, date of death and certifying details from the pre-provided Texas death certificate capture in the project uploads folder, when this item is reached. The capture is a lead only and is not established until its own record is confirmed (the statewide index entry and the certificate itself must agree). Its stated place of death, if it names a Texas county, selects which Texas county series and cemetery records to search next. The survey did not place the decedent in Texas (loc_002 notes the death place must be read from the capture).

Texas Deaths, 1977-1986 (collection 1930157) is name-searchable with images (loc_002). It is the only listed Texas death image set overlapping the early part of the window after 1977, so it can supply a certificate or register image once the index entry is found. Fallback to the Texas death index entry when that entry gives a 1977-1986 death year; not a standalone search for later years.

California Death Index, 1940-1997 (collection 2015582) is the statewide index that spans the 2 July 1962 move to Los Angeles (loc_003). Name-searchable. Its entry gives a year and county, which tests the Los Angeles death place directly. An entry is not itself a place-of-death proof; the Los Angeles County records (loc_003) carry the confirmation.

entry.jurisdiction: Lyon, Minnesota, United States (Marshall, Lyon County)
entry.rationale: Minnesota Death Index, 1908-2002 (collection 1937234) is the statewide Minnesota index and is name-searchable (loc_001). The tree's 1940 draft-registration and 1940 residence entries name Marshall, Watonwan County, and Madelia, Watonwan County (not Lyon). Marshall city lies in Lyon County, so the index hit must be read against the county recorded before assuming loc_001's Lyon County series applies. Confirm which Marshall, and do not apply Marshall County, Minnesota records to Marshall in Lyon County.

United States, Social Security Death Index (collection 1202535) is name-searchable and gives a death date and the last residence ZIP code where the person's Social Security record reached the death file. It can narrow the state before the state indexes are searched. It runs to 2014, so a death after that year is not covered and must rest on the state indexes and records. The index does not establish a place of death by itself.

Los Angeles City, California, index of deaths, 1877-1962 (FamilySearch Library catalog 1173324) is browse-only and ends at the 2 July 1962 move date (loc_003). It can only reach a death in the first half of 1962 or earlier, so it is a fallback for pli_004 for a 1962 death in the city and not for later deaths. Browse image by image; there is no name search.

Angelus-Rosedale Cemetery/Crematory Records, 1884-2002 (collection 3583819) is name-searchable (loc_003). A cemetery or crematory entry can give the date and place of death together, and it is the next check if pli_004 finds a Los Angeles County death. Also consider the Pierce Brothers mortuary death records 1950-1978 (catalog 771104) and the Rose Hills burial database (from 1914) if no cemetery entry turns up.

entry.jurisdiction: Lyon, Minnesota, United States (Marshall, Lyon County)
entry.rationale: Lyon County Courthouse, Clerk of District Court, 607 W Main St, Marshall MN (holds birth and death records from 1874 per loc_001). This is the county series for a Marshall death, but it is a request to the courthouse, not an online search; the survey did not confirm post-1955 access. Run only if pli_005 places the decedent in Lyon County or an obituary or other record does. Fallback for pli_005 if that index is negative.

Marshall Cemetery alphabetized index (catalog koha:525977, typescript about 1992) lists those interred in Marshall Cemetery. It is a finding aid for a burial that may follow a Marshall death, and it is not a digitized burial register. Its three numeric columns are unexplained, so read it as a lead. Fallback for pli_009 when the county series returns nothing.

entry.repository: Southwest Minnesota Historical Center / Southwest State University (obituary files)
entry.rationale: Marshall obituary files ca. 1985-1990 (catalog 409008) and the statewide Minnesota Obituaries 1865-2006 collection (2469546, name-searchable) cover a Marshall death of that period. The Marshall obituary volumes are name-indexed but not full-text searchable, so they must be browsed once the name is located. Relevant only if pli_005 or pli_009 suggests a Marshall death.

entry.repository: other: local upload of Find a Grave capture (uploads/findagrave-quass-54602333.pdf)
entry.rationale: Read the uploaded Find a Grave capture for the memorial's stated death date and place. A memorial is a secondary, user-submitted lead and is not evidence of death until the death date and place are confirmed by one of the record items above. Use it to choose the state and county to test; do not write its dates into the tree from this item alone.

Texas, Deaths, 1890-1977 (collection 1983324) is name-searchable with images and overlaps the 1962-1963 gap in the Texas index that begins in 1964 (loc_002). Fallback for pli_001 only for a death in 1962 or 1963; the collection ends in 1977, so it does not reach later deaths.

## Question
When and where did Kenneth Werner Quass (KNS4-P6W), born 4 December 1917 in Sumner, Bremer County, Iowa, son of Ralph Kennedy Quass and Emma Wilhelmina Nehls, die?

## Answer in brief
The evidence points to a death on 17 September 1982, but only as a possible answer. The place of death is not established; the finding for place is not proved. This is a wrap-up conclusion, written while important records remain unsearched.

## Date: possible
The Find a Grave Index entry for Kenneth Werner Quass, Sr ("Find a Grave Index", FamilySearch, record ark:/61903/1:1:QVK1-PM77) gives a death of 17 Sep 1982, birth 04 Dec 1917 and burial at Madelia, Watonwan, Minnesota. It is a derivative index of indeterminate quality: it names no informant and the birth is inferred. It is linked to the subject with confidence (exact full name, birth date gap of 0 years, same-person score 0.958), so it is the only record tied to the subject's identity. The Texas Death Index entry ("Texas, Death Index, 1903-2000", record ark:/61903/1:1:VZZJ-TBB) gives Kenneth Quass, male, died 17 Sep 1982, Tarrant, Texas, and was classed primary for the death fact (certifying official). Two sources agreeing on a date would normally strengthen it, but the Texas entry is not linked to the subject (same-person score 0.35: no middle name, no birth date, no parents). Its date agreement therefore cannot be counted as independent support, and the subject's date rests on one index of indeterminate quality. The coincidence of surname, given name and exact date is suggestive, which is why the date is possible rather than not proved.

## Place: not proved
Three leads name Tarrant County, Texas: the Texas index entry, the Find a Grave memorial and an uploaded Ancestry index capture. The linked Find a Grave index entry instead supplies only a Minnesota burial (Madelia), which is a burial place and not a place of death. A contributor note on the memorial says the Texas place is false, describing a death on a Miami-to-San Diego flight that landed at Dallas, with burial in Madelia. That note is unsourced and has not been extracted or weighed as evidence. The uploaded memorial and certificate captures were not read as evidence. A Texas death followed by a Minnesota burial is plausible but undocumented. No place of death is concluded and nothing is written to the tree for it.

## Open candidate h_001
Hypothesis h_001 (active, not adopted) asks whether the Kenneth Quass of the Texas index is the subject. It is unresolved. It would be settled by: (1) the readable Texas death certificate showing parents (Ralph Quass and Emma Nehls), birth date or birthplace and informant; (2) a Texas residence before 1982; (3) an obituary or Social Security record giving the middle name Werner and birth date 4 December 1917; (4) the Find a Grave Texas-place source and contributor note, extracted and weighed. Minnesota death or burial records at Madelia or Watonwan County, and Los Angeles County records (the subject was in Los Angeles in 1962), could independently establish the place. No conflict is registered; the disagreement over place is an unresolved candidate question, not an adjudicated conflict.

## Tree
The tree already carries Death F2 (17 Sep 1982, from the Find a Grave Index, source S2) and Burial F1 (Madelia, Minnesota). No place of death and no Texas fact is encoded. These are evidence facts, not a concluded proof.

## Limits
The unsearched records listed in the search summary can change this answer; the finding is possible, not settled.

The survey covered Los Angeles County for 1962 to 2024, and it found the records that would hold a death for this man: the statewide California Death Index for 1940 to 1997, which spans the whole move window, plus county, city and cemetery files. The county Recorder holds death records, and the city index of deaths runs only to 1962, the year of the move. The most likely sources are the Lyon County Courthouse clerk, which holds birth and death records from 1874, and the statewide Minnesota death indexes and certificates on FamilySearch.
